messages:
amy-cs: Hi team — acme-inc hit a burst of 429s during a live demo tonight. They say their monthly tokens should've refilled at local midnight but requests started failing ~22:05 their time. Org: org_86b4. Can we confirm reset timing and whether a retry storm double-counted?

jake-eng: thx. can you paste a sample request/response and the customer timezone?

amy-cs: PST. sample response attached by customer:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "quota_exhausted",
  "detail": "monthly token bucket empty",
  "reset_at": "2026-03-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

liam-sre: quick note — reset_at in response is canonical (UTC). if customer is PST, their local midnight is 08:00 UTC, so that doesn't line up with 22:05 PST. need to check if they hit a short-lived cap earlier (consumption spike).

amy-cs: customer says they were doing long-running streaming + frequent reconnects during demo (multiple presenters). they saw 429s for ~15m then it cleared. no plan change in last 30d per customer.

jake-eng: can you ask for the request-id headers or timestamps? also whether they used org keys vs service keys. retry loops can burn tokens fast.

amy-cs: they sent X-Req-Id: req_0a9e and timestamps in their logs: 2026-03-17T22:05:07-08:00 -> first 429, then a flurry every ~2s for 12m.

billing-bot: FYI — this tenant's monthly refill schedule: monthly_bucket_refill = 00:00 UTC on the 1st of each month. UI quota display caches for 300s; API checks real-time.

liam-sre: pulled metrics for org_86b4: sudden token drain at 2026-03-18T06:05:03Z (~22:05 PST) with ~1.2M tokens used in 12 minutes. pattern matches a retry storm + streaming window overlap.

jake-eng: that consumption would definitely preempt the upcoming refill. also check whether they were on a trial promo with separate top-up; those can expire at month boundary causing unexpected draws.

amy-cs: customer confirms no promo. they did mention they toggled a presenter in the middle of the demo which kicked off reconnects.

dev-bot: note created: INCIDENT-8342 — temporary quota lift requested for org_86b4. linked billing audit job queued.

liam-sre: mitigation plan: (1) temp quota bump for 24h so their demo can finish, (2) run audit to confirm no double-counting on reconnects, (3) recommend client change: exponential backoff + idempotent connect token to avoid duplicate streams.

amy-cs: customer asked whether their UI should have shown low quota earlier. what's the race?

billing-bot: UI uses an edge cache that updates every 5m; if usage spikes quickly, UI can lag behind API enforcement. this is expected behavior but we should doc it.

jake-eng: for reproducibility, ask customer to run this against their long-running scenario and capture headers:
```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <ORG_KEY>" 
  -H "X-Debug-Request: 1" 
  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -d '{"prompt":"stream test","stream":true}'
```
collect X-Req-Id and server Date.

amy-cs: I shared the mitigation and repro steps. customer accepted the temporary bump and sent the requested debug on the next run. they also attached the X-Req-Id for us (req_0a9e).

liam-sre: audit shows repeated reconnects with new session tokens every ~2s from same client IP; each reconnect allocated a fresh token-draw. not a double-count bug server-side, but aggressive client behavior.

amy-cs: relayed to customer and recommended backoff + reuse of session token. they appreciated the quick bump. :thumbsup:

jake-eng: moving to postmortem: add doc blurb about UI cache lag and recommend a best-practice for streaming clients. also consider a short lived heuristic detection for reconnect storms to apply a gentler rate-limit.

amy-cs: customer follow-up: demo finished, they used the bump and were able to complete. closing on our side after monitoring period. ticket INCIDENT-8342 -> CLOSED in support tracker.

liam-sre: note for ops — no server-side quota reset bug found. root cause: high burst consumption from client reconnects + UI cache lag.

amy-cs: thanks all, marking resolved.
